youtube.title: The Night Before Challenger, Engineers Begged NASA Not to Launch
youtube.description:
Six months before Challenger, Morton Thiokol engineer Roger Boisjoly warned that failing O-ring seals could cause "a catastrophe of the highest order." The night before launch, Thiokol's engineers recommended against flying in the cold. Managers reversed them. 73 seconds after liftoff, Challenger broke apart.

📂 Case File #038: The Challenger Warning

Sources: Report of the Presidential Commission on the Space Shuttle Challenger Accident (Rogers Commission), https://www.nasa.gov/history/rogersrep/v1appd.htm ; NPR, "Remembering Roger Boisjoly" (2012).
Images: NASA / Kennedy Space Center (public domain); US Senate hearing record (public domain).
Narration voice: AI.
